title: For a four-term inverse system of complexes the zeroth cohomology of the limit is the limit of the zeroth cohomologies under two vanishing hypotheses
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an inverse system of four-term complexes of abelian groups, denotes its limit and the inverse systems of cohomologies, and assumes that (A^{-2}_n) and (A^{-1}_n) have vanishing R^1 lim and that (H^{-1}_n) has vanishing R^1 lim; it concludes that H^0 = lim H^0_n (source lines 23022-23038). The proof is a spectral sequence computation carried out on both sides. It represents the system as an object K of the derived category of inverse systems of abelian groups, and computes H^0(R lim K) using both spectral sequences of the two-variable spectral sequence lemma, adding a footnote explaining that the use of these spectral sequences requires Ab(N) to have enough injectives, that an inverse system of abelian groups is injective exactly when each term is injective and the transition maps are split surjections, and that every system embeds in one of these, with the details stated to be omitted (proof lines 23041-23050). The first spectral sequence has the displayed E_1 page with terms R^1 lim A^0_n and R^1 lim A^1_n in the top row and A^{-2}, A^{-1}, A^0, A^1 in the bottom row, with horizontal differentials and all higher differentials zero (proof lines 23051-23058). The second has the displayed E_2 page whose bottom row consists of the limits of the cohomology systems and whose top row consists of their first derived limits, and it degenerates there (proof lines 23059-23068). Comparing the two computations of the single group H^0(R lim K) under the stated vanishing hypotheses gives the conclusion (proof lines 23068-23069). The non-routine content is the double spectral sequence comparison together with the injectivity remark that legitimises it.
